_note: SHAPE REFERENCE, NOT CONTENT. Invented for this purpose -- no page of any textbook is behind it, and it must never be copied into a real assessment. It exists because a field list tells an author which keys to write and nothing at all about how much to write in them. Every rule wslint enforces is visible here at least once: a question with an illustration split into groups of four, an open-personal question that carries a model answer instead of a key, a directive kept off the child's sheet, and per-question marks that add up to the stated total. Kept lint-clean by test_cbrief.py, so it cannot rot into an example of the wrong thing.

generated.title: Chapter Worksheet — A Day at the Farm
generated.instructions: Read each question carefully. Do your best work.

questions.marking: 2 marks for Cow. No half marks.
common_errors: picks Hen because it is also a farm animal

questions.childText: A baby cat is called a ______.
questions.marking: 2 marks for kitten; 1 mark for a clear phonetic attempt such as 'kiten'.

questions.childText: Draw a line to match each animal to its home.
common_errors: joins every animal to the barn

questions.childText: There are 4 ducks in one pond and 3 ducks in another. How many ducks in all?

illustration.caption: two ponds, ducks drawn as separate groups

questions.marking: 2 marks for 7; 1 mark for a correct count shown on the picture with a wrong total.
common_errors: counts one pond only and answers 4

questions.childText: Draw the animal you liked best on the farm.
questions.directive: Let children draw without naming an animal for them.
questions.model_solution: Any recognisable farm animal, drawn with at least one identifying feature (a comb, a tail, wings).
questions.marking: 2 marks for a recognisable farm animal; 1 mark for an attempt.

questions.childText: The farmer has 5 eggs. He sells 2. How many eggs are left?
questions.marking: 2 marks for 3; 1 mark for showing 5 - 2 with a wrong answer.
common_errors: adds instead of subtracting and answers 7

questions.childText: Write one sentence about what the farmer does in the morning.
questions.answer: Any sentence naming a morning farm task, e.g. 'He feeds the hens.'
questions.marking: 2 marks for a full sentence, 1 for a phrase, 1 extra for a capital letter and a full stop.

questions.childText: Name two animals you saw at the farm.
questions.answer: Any two of: cow, hen, horse, duck, bee, cat.
